Tools.ChangesRecentInput.description: List the deploy-like changes nami saw in the resource attributes services send, newest first, in the window (since, default the last hour): a new commit (vcs.ref.head.revision), a new service.version, a new deployment.environment.name, or a changed cicd.* attribute. Use it to ask whether something changed shortly before errors or latency began. It reads only what the services reported; it does not ask a deployment system. from is absent when this is the first value nami saw for that service, which is not necessarily a deploy.

Tools.ErrorsRecentInput.description: Group the errors recorded in the window (since, default the last hour) by error type and operation, most frequent first, with first and last occurrence, a count and one example trace ID. Three things count as an error: a log record named exception, an exception event on a span, and a span with status error that recorded no exception. A plain log line at ERROR severity is not an error here; find those with logs_search. No stack traces are returned: pass example_trace_id to traces_get to read the exception event and the spans around it. operation is the span name, or log when the log record has no span.

Tools.LogsSearchInput.description: Find log records whose body contains query as literal, case-sensitive text (not a regular expression, no wildcards), newest first, in the window (since, default the last hour). Only the body is searched, not attributes, severity or the service name; narrow by service with service. Each record has its timestamp, severity, body, service and, when the log was written inside a span, trace_id and span_id for traces_get. Prefer several short, distinctive queries (an error code, an exception class name) over one long sentence.

Tools.SourcesStatusInput.description: List every service that has sent telemetry to nami, and for each of its three signals (traces, metrics, logs) whether it is active or silent. A signal is active when something arrived at or after since (default: the last hour) and silent otherwise; a silent signal carries silent_for and, if it was ever seen, last_seen. Call this first: it tells you which services exist (the values service accepts in every nami tool) and whether missing evidence means nothing happened or nothing was sent. nami stores metrics but has no tool that reads metric values. Rows are ordered by service name.

Tools.TracesGetInput.description: Read one trace by its 32-character lowercase hex trace ID: its root span, duration, services, error flag and every span with attributes, events (including exception events) and links. Use it after errors_recent, traces_slowest or logs_search gave you a trace ID. The trace is read whole whatever since says, up to the snapshot; with service, it is found only when one of its spans is from that service. Spans are ordered by start time and paged: when next_cursor is present, call again with it to read the next spans. To keep the answer small, pass fields, for example ["trace_id","root_span","span_count","duration_ns","has_error"] without spans.

Tools.TracesSlowestInput.description: Rank the traces that started in the window (since, default the last hour) by duration, longest first, and return up to limit of them (default 10, at most 100) with trace ID, root operation, duration in milliseconds, start time and status (error if any span failed). Use it for latency questions; for failures start with errors_recent. operation keeps only traces whose root span has exactly this name (case-sensitive; take names from an earlier traces_slowest or traces_get answer). Pass a trace_id from the answer to traces_get for the spans.
